author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
Thanks — I think the $740 difference comes entirely from how each engine characterizes the TAXSIM `pensions` field on the AR1000F.

PE puts the $89k on Line 18A/18B ("employment-related pension plans/qualified IRAs"), which gets the $6,000-per-spouse exemption under A.C.A. §26-51-307. The TaxAct PDF puts the same income on Line 16 ("lump-sum distributions, annuities, and traditional IRA distributions"), which isn't eligible for the exemption.

Under the AR1000F instructions, the line-18 exemption and the "65 Special" $29 credit are mutually exclusive — page 12 says: *"Any taxpayer age 65 or over not claiming a retirement income exemption on line 18 is eligible for an additional $29 (per taxpayer) tax credit."* So PE's path = $12k exemption + $174 personal credit; TaxAct's path = no exemption + $232 personal credit.

The diff reconciles cleanly to your observation that it isn't just a flat-rate effect: $798 of bracket savings from removing $12k of taxable income (the step-bracket effect is what makes it >$480 at flat 4%), minus $58 of extra personal credit = $740, exactly the observed gap.

On which characterization is correct: §26-51-307 covers "public or private employment-related retirement systems, plans, or programs," which is what "pension" typically means. For a generic TAXSIM `pensions` field, Line 18A seems like the conventional default — does that match your reading?

References:
- 2024 AR1000F & AR1000NR Instructions: https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024_AR1000F_and_AR1000NR_Instructions.pdf
- A.C.A. §26-51-307: https://law.justia.com/codes/arkansas/title-26/subtitle-5/chapter-51/subchapter-3/section-26-51-307/
- A.C.A. §26-51-501: https://law.justia.com/codes/arkansas/title-26/subtitle-5/chapter-51/subchapter-5/section-26-51-501/
